content.text: {"statements":{"L6.1":{"established":"yes","quote":"We next show that $a_1,a_2,\\ldots$ are exactly the members of $S$ that are at least $a_1$, in increasing order.","note":"The subsequent minimality argument proves the characterization for every integer at least a_1."},"L6.2":{"established":"no","quote":null,"note":"The claimed finite-blocker fact is false; its pruning argument does not justify finiteness and no valid large-prime erasure is proved."},"L6.3":{"established":"partial","quote":"Since the terms of the sequence are the increasing enumeration of $S$ from $a_1$ onward, the $T$-th term after $a_n$ is therefore $a_n+L$.","note":"The from-n=1 counting argument is correct conditionally, but the finite modulus L comes solely from the false transversal lemma."}},"S_ref":0,"notes":"Characterization is valid. The proof’s essential finiteness lemma is false, so the finite union of divisibility sets and hence its modulus are unsupported; only the conditional periodicity assembly is sound."}
